title: OC6 Huli Instruction Video Released
excerpt: In 2025, the Hood River Outrigger Canoe Club filmed a comprehensive OC6 huli instruction video at the Hood River Aquatic Center and on the Columbia River. The video focuses on safe, practical…
html:
In 2025, the Hood River Outrigger Canoe Club filmed a comprehensive OC6 huli instruction video at the Hood River Aquatic Center and on the Columbia River. The video focuses on safe, practical techniques for recovering from a capsize and getting paddlers back into the canoe efficiently and calmly. Using clear demonstrations, the crew walks through key steps including counting out paddlers after a huli, paddle stowage, righting the canoe, stabilizing on the ama side, and re entering in a controlled order that prioritizes safety and stability.

The video also covers multiple re entry methods, including leg driven climbs, heel hooks, use of the iako for leverage, and optional tools like step straps for paddlers who need additional support. Special attention is given to cold water considerations, head protection during a huli, and reducing water intake while righting the canoe. The emphasis throughout is on staying calm, taking time, and using whatever techniques are available to get everyone back in safely.

This instructional resource was made possible through a generous grant from the Pacific Northwest Outrigger Racing Canoe Association and is intended to support paddlers across the region in building confidence, safety, and readiness for real world conditions on the water.

title: 2023 President’s Welcome
excerpt: We are looking forward to a productive new year with a full race calendar and a proposed association wide open house month in April.
html:
May 2023

Paddling season is here, and we are emerging from the COVID blues. So far, our events are well attended and there are lots of new paddlers enjoying our sport.

PNWORCA has been busy with the onboarding of new officers. Drea Park has accepted an offer to join the Officers as Sergeant at Arms. Her appointment requires Board approval and that will be on the next Board meeting agenda.

We have hired a new web administrator, Kjirstin Bentson, to assume the role that Kate Goudschaal filled along with PNWORCA Secretary, for the last four years. Due to a resignation, she has agreed to also assume the Secretary role as a contractor. We continue to seek members to serve as Secretary and can elect an incumbent at our Fall meeting.

Three Member Grants were approved and funded. Hui Heihei purchased a portable public address system for use by all clubs. The unit is the size of a suitcase and is completely self-contained. Contact me if your event can benefit from this new equipment. Kikaha’s request for huli safety training was also funded. The event was held in April with eight clubs and a hundred paddlers enjoying the waters of Mt Tahoma High School pool. Finally seed money was provided to Zamboanga for a Kalama Heritage Days canoe race to be held August 5th.

Finally mark your calendar for our Fall annual meeting on November 4.

IMUA
Andy Michels, President
PNWORCA

Duties of the Sergeant at Arms position include:

Per the PNWORCA Bylaws: The Sergeant-at-Arms shall assist the President in maintaining order and decorum at meetings and shall monitor attendance at such meetings. In addition, the Sergeant-at-Arms shall maintain a current list of all Association property, shall be responsible for storage of Association property, and shall check the condition, repair or replacement of such property. 

Equipment storage and maintenance is the largest responsibility of this role. Those specific duties include:

  • Arrangement of storage for all PNWORCA owned equipment (primarily all the sprint equipment).  
  • Work with the sprint race directors to either transport the equipment to the race and back to storage or give them access to the storage unit for them to handle these duties.
  • Yearly inspection of the equipment to verify its good order and needs for repairs.
  • Coordinate and required repairs of the equipment.

title: Statement from the PNWORCA Executive Board On COVID-19
imageAlt: Special Statement From the PNWORCA Executive Board
excerpt: As we find ourselves in the midst of the COVID-19 global pandemic, it should come as no surprise that our current paddling season is both in flux and at risk of not moving forward as we all would…
html:
To our PNWORCA paddlers and extended family,

As we find ourselves in the midst of the COVID-19 global pandemic, it should come as no surprise that our current paddling season is both in flux and at risk of not moving forward as we all would have hoped.  We understand that there is an undeniable urge to paddle and come together to share experiences with each other and spend time on the water as a family. Unfortunately, the reality of our current situation prohibits us from enjoying paddling as we are used to. 

In response to the coronavirus pandemic, the PNWORCA Executive Board is making the following recommendations:

  • We must strictly adhere to current federal, state and local laws and recommendations regarding public gatherings when considering club practices and PNWORCA sanctioned races.
  • If during the 2020 paddling season new ordinances are in place which allow for gatherings large enough to host races, the PNWORCA Executive Board will support the individual decision of each Race Director on whether or not to host their race.
  • If the Executive Board is required to make a decision impacting the PNWORCA community, we will always act in the best interest of the health and safety of our paddling family. 

More information regarding current state laws and recommendations can be found at the following links:

https://coronavirus.wa.gov

https://govstatus.egov.com/or-covid-19

https://covid19.mt.gov

https://coronavirus.idaho.gov

https://coronavirus.utah.gov

As of May 11th, we have confirmation from Race Directors regarding the following races:

  • Rusty Iron race on April 25th: CANCELLED
  • Race Around the Island race on May 2nd:  CANCELLED
  • Manu Baker Sprint Race on May 16th: CANCELLED
  • Hui Heihei Silverdale Sprints on May 30th: CANCELLED
  • The Gorge Race on July 11th: CANCELLED
  • 2020 IVF World Sprints in Hilo in August: CANCELLED

Please stay healthy and look out for one another by practicing safe, responsible behaviors to help end this current pandemic. Our families will always have priority to us as we work together to overcome this. We will all be back out on the water together in a short time!

If you have any questions, please feel free to contact any PNWORCA Executive Board member directly.

Stay safe and stay healthy, 
Your PNWORCA Executive Board

Ernie Wong, President
Steve Pietila, Vice President
Jason Zimmermann, Sergeant at Arms
Andy Michels, Treasurer
Kate Goudschaal, Secretary
Tyler Irwin, Race Chair
Sabine Jessel, IVF/USAORCA Representative
